## Welcome

This app covers the nine lectures of STA520: from the biology (DNA, RNA, proteins, mutations) through genetic association (GWAS) and causal inference (Mendelian randomization) to high-dimensional omics, proteomics and polygenic risk scores. One clinical example runs through the whole course: the **LDLR–PCSK9–LDL cholesterol** pathway.

## How to study with it

1. **Read a lecture.** Every topic section has a status control under its heading: **Not reviewed / Reviewed / Confident**. Click as you go.
2. **Answer the quizzes** inside each lecture and the **why-questions** and **spaced review** at the bottom.
3. **Start the [Exam practice](exam-practice.qmd) page with the instructor's 11 Lecture 7 example questions**, then practise calculations: drills that generate new numbers every time (Benjamini–Hochberg, Bonferroni, Hardy–Weinberg, OR from β, Wald ratio, IVW, F-statistic, allele alignment, PRS, log₂FC, quantile normalization, moderated t) plus 34 written exam-style questions with model answers.
4. **Go through [Martin's key concepts](key-concepts.qmd)**: 20 short modules for GWAS, MR and proteomics, one per concept on the list, then the [seminar questions](seminar-questions.qmd) with concept-level model answers.
5. **Prepare for the computer exercises** with [Computer exercises: concepts](computer-exercises.qmd): QC, PLINK output, clumping, allele alignment and MR interpretation on made-up data.
6. **Practise the professor's word list** with the [flashcards](vocabulary.qmd): write a sentence with each word, then compare.
7. **Check the [dashboard](dashboard.qmd)** to see what is left: exam topics in priority order (🎯 🎓 🔑 🗣️ 📌), then topics with unclear status.
8. Look up terms in the [glossary](glossary.qmd) or use **search** (top right). Searching "PCSK9" finds it in Lectures 1, 2, 3, 6 and 8.

## Exam flags

What is known about the exam: the **written exam** covers Lecture 7 (🎯) and the words and concepts on the professor's list for Lectures 1–3 (🎓). For GWAS, MR and proteomics, **Martin's key-concepts list** (2 October) names 20 concepts (🔑). GWAS and MR are also examined at the **seminar** (🗣️), and seminar content **can also come on the written exam** (corrected 2 October; an earlier version of this app said it would not). Do not focus on specific medicines, mutations or the running examples.

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| <span class="flag-badge flag-instructor">🎯 Instructor-flagged EXAM</span> | The slide carried the literal "EXAM" marker from the instructor (**Lecture 7 only**). Highest priority. |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-inferred">📌 Likely exam-relevant (AI-inferred)</span> | Inferred from definitions, formulas and worked examples. **Not confirmed by the instructor.** |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-professor">🎓 On the professor's list</span> | The section covers words or concepts on the professor's exam list for Lectures 1–3 (lecture notes, 29 September). Practise them with the [flashcards](vocabulary.qmd). **On the written exam.** |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-professor_unsure">🎓 On the professor's list (use uncertain)</span> | On the professor's list, under "uncertain about use" (checking HWE, checking SNP–phenotype association). |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-unclear">❔ Exam status unclear</span> | GWAS/MR/PRS theory that is neither on Martin's key-concepts list nor part of the computer exercises and seminar questions (for example covariates, Bradford Hill, polygenic risk scores, protein MR). Not confirmed either way. |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-keyconcept">🔑 Martin's key concepts</span> | The section covers one of the 20 concepts on Martin's key-concepts list for GWAS, MR and proteomics (2 October). Each has its own short module on [Martin's key concepts](key-concepts.qmd). **Exam-relevant.** |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-seminar">🗣️ Seminar topic (can also come on the exam)</span> | Covered by computer exercises 1–2 and the [seminar questions](seminar-questions.qmd). Examined at the seminar, and seminar content **can also come on the written exam**. |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-example">Example, not exam focus</span> | The course's running examples (PCSK9, LDLR, specific medicines and mutations). The lecturer said not to learn them specifically. |

::: {.callout-important}
## Instructor's example exam questions included
The 11 questions from **"Lecture 7 - questions.pdf"** are on the [Exam practice](exam-practice.qmd) page, with model answers written for this app. The computer exercise instructions are still missing; see [About the content](about.qmd).
:::

Code blocks marked *Run Code* are interactive: R runs in your browser, no installation needed. The first run on a page takes a few seconds while R loads.
